text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- The government has started cutting budget expenditure in line with figures put forward by the finance ministry without waiting for a formal approval by the Duma.
- Russia will sign a deal with De Beers only when the Yakutian diamond-mining company ARS makes its balance sheets absolutely transparent to the government.

- The Duma has approved a law granting tax breaks to institutional shareholders on profits they may acquire from an increase in the value of shares they own after a revaluation of capital funds of the companies who issued the shares.
- An overwhelming majority of Duma deputies see the way out of the budget crisis in an immediate increase in money supply.
- Moscow confectionary giant Babayevskoye is planning to acquire another big confectioner, Konditer, to form a holding company under the auspices of Inkombank.
- Shareholders in Nizhegorodnefteprodukt have ruled that the company should keep all its filling stations.

- St Petersburg commercial banks Promstroybank and Petrovsky have bought 51 percent of the shares in local arms producer Arsenal, putting an end to a long-running argument over who will manage the company.
- The Russian republic of Chuvashia has chosen Sberbank as its main partner on the financial market.
- Russian ONEXIMBank-MFK group stands to become the biggest shareholder in Belarussian Minskkomplexbank once the latter brings its statutory capital up to 5 million Ecus.
SEVODNYA
- Moscow city authorities are planning to change the system of taxation of casinos to increase their budget revenues.
- The Duma has started work on a draft law which is supposed to make it more difficult for the government to cut budget spending without the deputies' consent.
- The government has made its first budget cuts without waiting for the green light from the Duma.
- The Russian energy sector is in for a big shake-up which will probably break up one of the biggest monopolies, Unified Energy Systems.
- First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov says Russian prize gas giant Gazprom will have to work to create conditions for the development of other industries.
- A joint Russian-Finnish-German consortium will build a car plant near St Petersburg.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA

- The scale of reforms forced upon Gazprom is so big that it makes one wonder whether those who promote them are fully aware of the consequences such deep restructuring could have for the country as a whole.
- The Supreme Arbitration Court has ruled that statutory documents of St Petersburg gold-mining company Lenzoloto null-and-void, de facto bringing the company back into state ownership.
- Russian telecommunications giant Svyazinvest will shortly sell 49 percent of its shares at an auction.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- President Yeltsin has signed several decrees aimed at increasing efficiency in the use of public money.
- First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais says Russian republic Yakutia has a future and should seek an international credit rating.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS

- The Russian government, which has rarely been able to stick to budget figures for this year, has decided to cut expenditure, a move which met fierce resistance from opposition deputies in parliament.
--Andrei Shukshin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
